summary: Stefan Anacker was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Alex Wayman from circa 1965 to 1970.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. After completing his dissertation at the University of Washington (c. 2002–2009), he held posts there, at the University of Copenhagen, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefan Larsson is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Stockholm University (c. 2003–2009) under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, and later completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Berkeley (c. 2010–2012).
Stefan Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin from 1987 to 1995 and at Heidelberg University in 1995.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen from circa 2013 to 2020 before taking a post at SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. After completing his PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (c. 1995–1999), he held posts at Soka University, IRIAB, the University of Padua, Ca' Foscari, and the University of Oxford.

Steffen Döll is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. Circa 2015, he held posts at the University of Hamburg as Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism and as Series Editor for Hamburg Buddhist Studies.

Stella Kramrisch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Vienna (c. 1914–1919), she held posts at the University of Calcutta (c. 1923–1950) and the University of Pennsylvania (c. 1950–1972).

Sten Konow was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel. His career included posts at the Berlin State Library, Archaeological Survey of India, and universities of Oslo, Hamburg, and Visva-Bharati.

Stephan Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson from circa 1968 to 1970. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1971 to 1979.

Stephan Conermann is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kiel from circa 1984 to 1990 and became a professor at the University of Bonn around 2003.

Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia from circa 1978 to 1983, with teachers including Daniel L. Overmyer, Yoshitaka Iriya, and Shoko Kanaoka.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She served as Professor of Environmental Studies at the University of Vermont from circa 1991 to 2015.
Stephanie Roemer is a Tibetology scholar. She completed her studies from circa 2004 to 2007 under the doctoral supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale University from circa 1972 to 1977. She held a post at Harvard University (c. 1999–2002) and an editorial board post at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 2002.
Stephen A. Murphy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London from circa 2004 to 2010, completing an MA.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (c. 1970–1977). He held professorships at the University of Kansas (c. 1977–1995) and the University of Richmond (c. 1995–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Satya Narayan Goenka, Ngawang Dhargyey, and Geshe Rabten, and also studied at Songgwangsa under Kusan Sunim from 1981 to 1984.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at the University of Colombo (c. 1996–1997), Missouri State University (c. 2005–2009), and Ruhr University Bochum in 2011.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University (PhD c. 1980–1986). He held posts at Middlebury College (c. 1986–1988) and Princeton University, where he became D.T. Suzuki Professor.
